subject: Ordering of x axis depends on facet_wrap

messages.author: c33ade33b8da6be5
messages.subject: Ordering of x axis depends on facet_wrap
parts:
Hi all,

I've just recently started using R and ggplot2, but I'm already a fan.
However, I've ran into a problem with facet_grid. Even though I have
an ordered variable I'm using for my x axis, facet_grid ignores this
order in a specific case.

My dataset exists of 5 columns, of which I want to plot a bargraph in
a grid. I'm using:
d<-ggplot(uascen.m2, aes(x=answer, y=value, fill=variable))
+geom_bar(stat="identity")
d + facet_grid(scenarioID~variable, scales="free") +
opts(legend.position = "none", axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=-90,
hjust=0))

However, the resulting plot shows that the order in the first column
of the grid is not as it should be. "Very unrealistic" should be
positioned after "Not realistic". However, when I change the facets
to:
facet_grid(.~variable, scales="free"), the order is respected.

Is there a way to solve this problem?

You can find the dataset here: http://ggplot2.googlegroups.com/web/uascen.m2.rda

Thanks very much!

Thijs

messages.author: c33ade33b8da6be5
messages.subject: Re: Ordering of x axis depends on facet_wrap
parts:
Hi Hadley and others,

I've added the dataset as a csv.

Below is the reproducible example:

library(gdata)
library(ggplot2)
uascen.m4<- read.table("uascen.m4.txt", header=TRUE, sep=",",
na.strings="NA", dec=".", strip.white=TRUE)
uascen.m4$answer<-reorder.factor(uascen.m4$answer, new.order=c(5,4,3,6,2,1))
d<-ggplot(uascen.m4, aes(x=answer, y=value, fill=variable)) +
geom_bar(stat="identity")
d+ facet_grid(scenarioID~variable, scales="free") + opts(legend.position
= "none", axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=-90, hjust=0),
strip.text.y=theme_text(angle=-60, size=8))

This produces a bargraph with the answer "very unrealistic"in last
position, where ggplot ignores the order of the levels for this
variable. Removing scenarioID from the facet_grid, shows a correct
bargraph, however not with the right faceting.

I also tried reordering the data as suggested by Luciano Selzer
(thanks!) but that didn't help.

I think it is because the level "very unrealistic" only occurs in the
last level of scenarioID. But it's strange to me that the ordering is
not explicitly followed. Adding a zero as value for the combination of
"very unrealistic" and "Scenario 2" solves the problem of the ordering,
but shows a short bar where one should not occur.

I hope you can help me out!

Thijs
